reconcile.connective: Defenders answer that the Law was not abrogated but fulfilled — its force endures even as the new covenant brings it to its goal in Christ.

discrepancy.connective: Thomas Paine pressed the underlying objection: an immutable God cannot give one law in one age (the Old Testament) and a contrary law in another (the New), so the two-law scheme is self-refuting.

skeptic.name: Thomas Paine
skeptic.attribution: Thomas Paine (d. 1809), The Age of Reason (1794)

excerpts.excerpt_text: Although the new covenant fulfilled the Old Testament law and prophets, the law has not passed away …
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly answers Luke 16:16's 'until John' horn and the abrogation claim: the Law is fulfilled, not superseded or void — the core harmonizing move for whether the Law is still binding.

pd_work.resource: John Gill, Exposition of the Entire Bible (1746-63), on Luke 16:16
pd_work.author: John Gill
pd_work.note: Gill treats this passage directly, anticipating and rejecting the inference that 'the law and the prophets were until John' means the Law was 'abrogated and laid aside'; he argues it had 'their full accomplishment' in Christ. (Haley's coverage of this specific passage could not be confirmed; this harmonizing commentator is surfaced on the row.)
